macro.note: Dallas Fed-confirmed; July production was 10.1. There are no major US economic reports Monday. What actually matters about the date is that it is the August close: month-end index rebalancing and settlement flows run through the tape, so Monday's price action carries less information than usual. Aug 31 is a UK bank holiday, which thins London liquidity, but US markets hold a normal full session - Labor Day is Monday Sept 7, verified on the NYSE, Nasdaq and FINRA calendars. 13-week and 26-week bill auctions

macro.event: ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS job openings
macro.note: NY Fed calendar-confirmed for Sept 1 at 10:00 ET. July ISM manufacturing was 55.6% and June JOLTS openings 7.359mn, both from the issuing agencies; TE carries indicative consensus of 55.0-55.3 and 7.39-7.40mn, treated as provisional. Disclosed: one aggregator places JOLTS on Sept 2 against four sources on Sept 1, and we could not confirm it on the BLS's own schedule page, which rendered only through mid-2026. Construction spending the same morning. Fed's Barr speaks - time conflicts between calendars at 9:05 AM and 1:05 PM, so neither is asserted. First hard data of September, two weeks before the Sept 15-16 FOMC

macro.event: Fed Beige Book; ADP employment 8:15 AM and factory orders
macro.note: Fed and ADP confirmed. July ADP was plus 44,000. The Beige Book is the last qualitative read the committee publishes before the September meeting, and after Friday it is the first chance to see whether the districts describe the inflation Warsh described

macro.event: ISM Services PMI; jobless claims, trade balance and revised productivity 8:30 AM
macro.note: NY Fed-confirmed. July ISM services was 54.1%. Revised productivity and unit labour costs land the same morning and matter more than usual now that the Chair has put the inflation burden on the central bank rather than on the labour market. Fed speakers Thursday are given as Waller on one calendar and Cleveland's Hammack plus Chicago's Goolsbee on another; both are reported, neither is reconciled

Triple-verified on the BLS empsit page and the September release schedule, and independently on the NY Fed calendar. Consensus is around plus 60,000 with unemployment at 4.1% - a Reuters poll reads plus 58,000 and 4.1%, one house reads plus 60,000 and 4.2%, so the range is named rather than a single figure asserted. July was MINUS 23,000 payrolls with a 4.1% unemployment rate. This is the single most consequential number between now and the Sept 15-16 FOMC, it lands eleven days before that decision, and it lands into pre-holiday liquidity on the Friday before the Sept 7 close. Reuters frames jobs plus Broadcom as the week's two hurdles

earnings.name: Dell Technologies
earnings.note: 4:30 PM ET Tuesday, IR-confirmed. The next real AI-server datapoint into a tape that just sold Marvell 10.28% for soft guidance. There are no noteworthy US earnings before Tuesday, which is worth stating rather than padding the list

earnings.name: MongoDB
earnings.note: 5:00 PM ET Tuesday, IR-confirmed. Enterprise software into the same guidance-punishment tape

earnings.name: Broadcom
earnings.note: Broadcom headlines the week's earnings and is the AI-silicon read-through that matters most after Marvell's 10.28% Friday drop and Nvidia's 4.58% give-back. Also due that week: Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler, Lululemon, HPE, GitLab, NetApp and Samsara. Date is per a week-ahead wire rather than an IR page, so treat the exact day as provisional
